page.layout: One page of text, verse set as stanzas, in one column. Running head at top, page number at top right. A rule separates the first verse block from the second. No marginal notes.

p.i: Tot sollibus mendacia vomis pe[?]toris: Fabelle capite erroribus tam turgido, Quam prominente adipis onuste farcina: In quo renatum Marcionem cernimus: Quo Nestorius & Eutyches ceu pronubo, Errore nexi dispari quantumlibet, Peperere monstrum Ubiquitatis impiæ: Quis hic furor? proie[?]ta quæ est audacia? Tractare sacra audere vos mysteria? Spondere Christi audere vos pacem gregi?

At ô beatæ principes Germaniæ, Mentita Jesum, quos adhuc fallit cohors, Prudentiæ cuius vel est sapientiæ, Satana ex magistro veritatem accersere? Sperare pacem litium ex fautoribus? Et posse fieri somniare ut indicent Lucem Tenebræ, Veritatem falsitas?

main_text.p: Dogmata qui dirimant inter pugnantia lites Hinc venit Pistor, venit & inde faber. Pontificis pinsit fermentum Pistor, ut inde In Cereris mutet fragmina parua Deum. At faber erranti cudit dum forcipe, corpus Fabricat immensum, quod sit ubique simul. Os hominum.quis enim tulerit de lumine cæcos Certantes tenebris implicitóque suis? Pistrinum Pistor potius dedatur in ar[?]um Ut male sanus suos trudere discat suos[?].

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout. Line 1 "pe[?]toris" and the "ct" ligature in "proie[?]ta" and "ar[?]um" are doubtful. The last word of the final line is smudged and read as "suos[?]". "hominum.quis" keeps the printed point. The ô and the accents on "implicitóque" are as printed. No marginal notes or catchword.
